column36: Talil is working on an ambitious research project which aims to simultaneously destroy tumors and genetically modify the cell in the tumor periphery to produce potent immunotherapy compounds using pulsed electric fields. The goal is to treat the primary tumor and train the immune system to target distant metastatic disease.  To prepare for this work, Talil shadowed my students in the lab for the last two semesters where he learned basic mammalian cell culture and observed clinical oncology cases. This summer, through his participation in an REU, he has been working closely with a postdoc to clone and expand DNA plasmids and treat tumors in an in vivo model of disease. The team has been impressed with his effort so far and we are looking forward to having him continue working on this project.
column37: The proposed research project is ambitious and involves evaluating the anti-tumor effect of DNA immunotherapies using both in vitro and in vivo models. Talil is currently receiving training on the most critical aspects of these studies and should be well prepared to conduct the most challenging aspects of the proposed work under the close guidance of a postdoctoral fellow. He is already growing his own cells and preparing concentrated DNA plasmids for experiments. He should have experience implanting, measuring, and treating tumors by the end of the summer. His effort so far provides me with a high degree of confidence in his ability to conduct the proposed work in collaboration with graduate students and postdocs in my lab.
column38: Talil will be mentored by a postdoctoral fellow in my lab (Christian Amador McRoberts) who is enthusiastic about Talil's continued participation in this work. Talil will attend my labs weekly lab meeting where he will have the opportunity to present his work and observe the work of others in the lab. I will routinely meet with Talil one on one to provide guidance. He will be encouraged to present his work at annual undergraduate research symposiums on campus. In addition, Talil will have the opportunity to shadow clinical cases where aspects of his research are already being used to treat oncology patients at the veterinary school.   Financial support for this project is provisioned via startup funds.
